claims.text: High-energy ball milling induces severe plastic deformation and produces a nanocrystalline or amorphous CoCrFeNiTi powder state.
Rapid Spark Plasma Sintering densifies the milled powder without prolonged thermal exposure.
Processing at 800–900 °C and high strain rate kinetically traps a nanocrystalline FCC solid solution with a minor BCC phase.
The proposed processing window avoids formation of a brittle Ti-rich HCP phase.
An equiatomic or near-equiatomic CoCrFeNiTi mixture has a high chemical potential for phase separation and HCP formation during slow cooling.
Milling at approximately 400 rpm with a 10:1 ball-to-powder ratio for 20–30 hours is sufficient to obtain a nanocrystalline or amorphous powder.
SPS at 800–900 °C, a heating rate above 100 °C/min, a dwell below 10 minutes, and 50–100 MPa pressure provides the required densification and phase retention.
A high plastic-flow strain rate during sintering closes pores before diffusion-driven phase separation occurs.
Nanocrystalline grain boundaries and stacking faults act as kinetic barriers to Ti segregation and HCP nucleation.
The rapid thermal cycle prevents formation of brittle Laves or Ti-rich HCP phases.
Rapid heating and high strain rate suppress Ti diffusion during SPS.
Grain-boundary pinning and solute drag stabilize the FCC solid solution.
A minor BCC phase arises from local compositional fluctuations and remains sufficiently dispersed to avoid a percolating brittle network.
The optimized material will have porosity below 1%, grain size below 100 nm, and less than 10% BCC in an FCC-dominated structure.
The optimized alloy will exceed 600 HV hardness and 10% elongation while having higher yield strength than a cast counterpart.
Conventional cast CoCrFeNiTi is a porous, homogeneous, soft, single-phase FCC alloy with hardness below 300 HV.
Temperatures above 950 °C or dwell times of at least 15 minutes cause HCP formation, grain growth, or phase separation.
Ti contents above 25 at% defeat kinetic suppression and lead to HCP formation.
Vickers indentation at a 500 g load and 15 s dwell time is proposed to test the hardness response of optimized and over-sintered samples.
A lack of significant hardness increase over the cast baseline would show that the grain-refinement or solute-strengthening mechanism is not operative.

contradictions.description: The boundary predicts that 1000 °C and a 30-minute dwell should promote HCP formation, but the falsification rule treats observation of more than 10% HCP under exactly that off-window condition as falsifying the hypothesis rather than confirming its stated boundary.

The hypothesis attributes hardness to both grain refinement and solute-related effects, but the proposed hardness comparison cannot distinguish these contributions; therefore, no hardness increase would not specifically establish that both mechanisms are inoperative.
